items.difficulty_reason: H2: The author builds the argument himself: he transposes via prop:tensor-Hom-cplx with B = k, shows the forgotten module I_k is injective because the forgetful functor has the exact left adjoint A tensor_k (.), uses the K-projectivity of X to get acyclicity of Hom^.(X tensor_R Y, I), and concludes X tensor_R Y is acyclic after testing against all injective I.

core_obligations: applies prop:tensor-Hom-cplx with B = k to get Hom^.(X tensor_R Y, I) = Hom^.(X, Hom^.(Y_k, I_k)) for an injective left A-module I viewed as a complex concentrated in degree zero
shows I_k is an injective k-module because the forgetful functor A Mod -> k Mod has the exact left adjoint A tensor_k (.), citing prop:adjoint-injective-projective and Li1
uses the acyclicity of Hom^.(Y_k, I_k) and the K-projectivity of X to get Hom^.(X tensor_R Y, I) acyclic
uses Hom(H^n(X tensor_R Y), I) = H^{-n}Hom^.(X tensor_R Y, I) = 0 for all injective I, plus the embedding of every left A-module into an injective, to conclude X tensor_R Y is acyclic

compared.title: Cycles of a K-flat acyclic complex with flat terms are flat
hypotheses_conclusions_evidence:
\label{lemma-K-flat-flat-acyclic}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$
be a K-flat, acyclic complex with flat terms. Then
$\mathcal{F} = \Ker(\mathcal{K}^n \to \mathcal{K}^{n + 1})$
is a flat $\mathcal{O}$-module.
